authority: _validation_registry.json is the executable source of truth; _repo_validation_matrix.json is generated from it.

common_sense_validation_policy.validate_lane: Validators inspect and report release-threatening integrity risk only. They do not build, publish, promote, absorb, apply, deploy, bootstrap runtimes, or mutate providers.
common_sense_validation_policy.execute_lane: Build, generate, normalize, repair, absorb, apply, publish, distribute, and self-heal commands must live in explicit build, execute, release, workflow, citation, apply, or repair lanes.
hard_fail_only_for: package integrity or wrong repo root
protected raw external agent artifact mutation unless explicitly quarantined
broken runtime/build contract for the actual app
unsafe public-surface claims or routing that can harm users

HARD_FAIL.meaning: Direct production, user-safety, evidence, route, workflow, build, or delivery threat; never cosmetic formatting.

STRONG_WARNING.meaning: Material quality, ingestion, indexing, accessibility, or performance degradation.

SOFT_WARNING.meaning: Maintainability, documentation, style, or low-risk quality concern.

INFO.meaning: Metric, observation, historical evidence, or optimization note.

validators.title: Delivered artifacts stay derivable from source
validators.risk_prevented: Prevents the frozen store becoming the only copy of delivered content. The semantic acceptance manifest was a per-run snapshot until 2026-09-01, so 249 accepted routes rebuilt 1,145,001 bytes lighter and the frozen restore hid it; the loss only became visible when a page was legitimately thawed. This proves data/release/accepted_page_artifacts.json still matches the accepted output, so every delivered artifact block is reproducible by a build.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: frozen-output-integrity proves the accepted bytes are intact; frozen-content-recoverability screens for routes that render more than their sections. Neither proves the artifact blocks on an accepted page can still be produced by a build, which is the condition that turned a routine thaw into silent content loss.

validators.title: A generated store contract does not expire at midnight
validators.risk_prevented: Prevents a generated store that carries a wall-clock generated_at inside the payload its own --check byte-compares. accepted-artifact-recovery and historic-artifact-recovery were both built that way: the stores were committed 2026-09-01 and from 00:00 UTC on 2026-09-02 the recomputed payload differed by exactly the date field, so a Tier 1 HARD_FAIL took down validate:release in the content-release lane, the query-evidence self-heal loop, and left Validate Repo red on an unabsorbed agent run - every day, because regenerating and committing the store buys exactly one day. Enrolment is derived from the registry itself so a future store of the same shape is covered when registered.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: accepted-artifact-recovery and historic-artifact-recovery each prove their own store is current, but both evaluate under a single SOURCE_DATE, so neither can tell a content change from a date rollover. self-heal-repair-contract proves a declared repair touches a file its validator reads, not that the validator returns a clock-independent verdict.

validators.title: Released-page admission reachability
validators.risk_prevented: The admission registry is built from published_urls.json, which is built from the routes the admission registry admits. That fixed point meant no page released after the 2026-06-19 baseline could ever enter it: eleven routes were promoted to live as ADMITTED, rendered as indexable HTML, and named by no sitemap, feed or llms export. Left in place it would have turned the newly wired 46-route backlog drain into 46 new orphans. This fails if any released, rendered, non-retired page is missing from the registry.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: rendered-route-admission-parity accepts a declared exclusion or a 301 as a complete answer, so a route can satisfy it forever while staying unreachable. sitemap-parity compares two artifacts derived from the same array and agrees with itself by construction. This one asks the different question: was the page the release lane actually released ever made findable?

validators.title: Citation-occupancy control separation and open-bucket integrity
validators.risk_prevented: Makes the occupancy probe's own control pair binding. Re-classifies every recorded citation host with the shared classifier and FAILS if any unrecognised host is counted as open, or if a recorded open/unclassifiable count does not match what the hosts derive. FAILS if a citation_occupancy number is published while the controls do not separate, or withheld while they do. Requires the unclassifiable slot count on every run. Hard-fails if it examines zero probes, zero cited hosts or zero controls.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: occupancy-probe-contract checks that the probe records a separation field and notes an inversion; it never failed on one, and it takes the probe's own arithmetic on trust. atlas-release-join checks a candidate's occupancy is traceable to a probe, not whether the probe measures openness at all. Neither re-derives the buckets from the recorded hosts, so a classifier that silently counted unrecognised hosts as open would pass both.

validators.title: No landed agent artifact sits pending longer than one release cadence
validators.risk_prevented: Velocity Content Release triggered only on the push that delivered a manifest, so an artifact got exactly one attempt. On 2026-09-02 the TRT run landed at 13:51, the lane ran at 13:52 on that sha and died at validate:release on the recovery-store midnight defect; absorption and publish never executed, the manifest stayed READY_FOR_ABSORPTION, and nothing retried because the trigger needs a NEW manifest. The defect was fixed and merged three hours later and the artifact was still stranded. query-evidence-refresh.yml - the repo’s single permitted scheduled committer - now also dispatches the release lane when a manifest is still unabsorbed, so the absorption pass can claim it; this fails if any manifest sits pending longer than the interval that schedule declares.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: agent-artifact-continuity fails on a run with no normalized output, but it fails the moment the raw drop lands and passes as soon as anything - including a human running the intake by hand inside an unrelated PR, which is what happened on 2026-09-02 - writes the normalized file. It measures a state, not an elapsed time, and it has no idea whether an automated lane will ever claim the run. This one derives its threshold from the workflow's own cron, so deleting the schedule fails the guard instead of disarming it.

lineage_policy.authority: _validation_registry.json is the executable source of truth for validation selection, dependency order, prerequisites, outputs, severity, and mutation boundaries.
lineage_policy.dependency_rule: Dependencies are included recursively and executed in topological order before dependents.
lineage_policy.prerequisite_rule: Missing required files trigger registered prepare_commands. Unregistered preparation is forbidden.
lineage_policy.mutation_rule: Validator commands may write only declared mutates_files. Source roots are hash-checked before and after each validator.
lineage_policy.output_rule: Declared produces_files must exist after a passing validator.

release_blocking_policy.clarification: Whitespace inside a URL or href remains a broken-link defect, not a formatting defect.

self_heal_policy.note: A validator may declare repair_command when a repair exists that targets the same defect it detects. The loop runs the profile, repairs what failed, and re-validates, up to --max attempts. Validators without a repair are reported by name rather than retried, because another identical pass would not change the result.
self_heal_policy.never: Do not pair a validator with a repair that merely makes it stop failing. A repair that hides a defect is worse than a red build.
